messages.subject: INLA output
parts:
Hi.

I'm pretty new to INLA, so please forgive me if my question is too naive.

I have fitted a state space model with the following code:

beta01.14 <- beta11.14 <- mat1.14$cohort
formula1.14st <- y ~ stage+f(beta01.14, model="ar1") + f(beta11.14, stage, model="ar1") 
res1.14 = inla(formula1.14, family="binomial", data = data.frame(mat1.14),Ntrials=n,
         control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE))

I have troubles interpreting the summary, in particular the hyper-paramter part:

Model hyperparameters:
                        mean    sd      0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant
Precision for beta01.14  0.4579  0.2405  0.1159     0.4195   1.0247  
Rho for beta01.14        0.9445  0.0305  0.8721     0.9495   0.9874  
Precision for beta11.14 13.2326  7.1730  3.6060    11.8803  30.8865  
Rho for beta11.14        0.8098  0.1017  0.5688     0.8262   0.9546  

I have learned from the latent models description (http://www.math.ntnu.no/inla/r-inla.org/doc/latent/ar1.pdf ) that for "ar1", the parameter phi is represented as theta_2, with the prior put on this theta_2, whose shortname is rho.

So my question: are the value I get in the summary (e.g. 0.9445 and 0.8098 above) estimates of phi or of theta_2 ? (the rho notation is confusing me).

Thank your for your help.

Eva Cantoni
